document.title: Summative Evaluation Plan and Formative Evaluation Summary - Infrared Forehead Thermometer

semantic_fragments.content: Objective: The objective of the Summative Evaluation is to confirm the safety and effectiveness of the user interface design of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer device.

Test Design: Develop a Summative Evaluation plan based on regulatory requirements and guidelines for usability and human factors engineering. Define specific tasks and scenarios that represent typical use cases and potential risks associated with the Infrared Forehead Thermometer device. Determine the appropriate sample size of representative users for testing.

Test Environment: Set up a controlled environment that mimics the intended use environment of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer device. Include appropriate equipment and support materials required for the evaluation.

Evaluation Metrics: Define relevant evaluation metrics, such as task success rates to complete tasks, error rates, and user satisfaction ratings. Establish acceptance criteria for each metric to determine if the user interface meets usability and safety requirements.

Analysis and Reporting: Analyze the data collected during the Summative Evaluation to identify any usability issues, use errors, or concerns related to device safety. Document the findings and recommendations for design improvements or risk mitigation measures.

Formative evaluations assess user interface designs during development to identify strengths and improvement opportunities. This is a mature device, the previous generation has been marketed in the EU, and the device is for home use. There are two formative evaluations for this device: the first stage is during design input, the second stage is during device validation. In the design input stage, cognitive walkthroughs and interviews from experienced engineers and customer representatives were conducted. The formative evaluation in this stage is input of hazard and hazard situation identified in the risk assessment. The Infrared Forehead Thermometer's user interface has been refined to ensure safety, usability, and alignment with user needs before moving on to summative evaluation. In the design validation stage, usability testing has been conducted on the finished device by representative operators.
